A1.justification: Both complete, readable 24-page PDFs describe the same CogNVS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–D support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CogNVS evaluations on Kubric-4D, ParallelDomain-4D and DyCheck, along with ablations and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds comparative runtime measurements and a qualitative panoramic-generation example.

M1.justification: Appendix B adds a progressive inference procedure: reconstruct previously generated views, then reproject and inpaint the next segment of a 360-degree trajectory. This extends inference beyond the original procedure; the core architecture, losses, training and test-time finetuning remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The four training datasets and three evaluation benchmarks are retained. New Figure 10 adds full 360-degree panoramic synthesis as a distinct test scenario using successive generated views, extending camera-trajectory coverage beyond the existing examples.

E2.justification: The accuracy-comparison baseline sets are unchanged. New Table 3 adds a DyCheck runtime comparison that includes GCD, previously compared only on the synthetic benchmarks, alongside MegaSAM, MoSca, Shape-of-Motion and TrajectoryCrafter.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the reported DyCheck evaluation resolution from 360 × 480 to 720 × 960. New analyses specify runtime evaluation on videos averaging 400 frames and panoramic generation using four 90-degree, 49-frame segments. The unchanged benchmark scores do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an optimization-versus-rendering runtime analysis and a maximum-view-angle case study with a panoramic example. Existing reconstruction-quality, masking, finetuning-duration, Top-k, background-stacking and noise-addition analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The Top-k sampling analysis is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests, and v2 adds no seed or repetition information.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are unchanged after matching table numbering. New Table 3 reports CogNVS finetuning at 140 minutes plus 5 minutes for inference, versus 66 minutes of optimization for MoSca and 237 for Shape-of-Motion. Figure 10 adds a qualitative panoramic result.

T1.justification: The rendering and covisibility definitions, diffusion objective, self-supervised training-pair construction and finetuning update are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: reconstruction-based inpainting, self-supervised training from 2D videos, test-time finetuning and strong zero-shot benchmark performance. Adding 'Test-Time' to the title emphasizes an existing contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly states failure beyond 90-degree deviations for inward-facing, object-centered views and suggests missing pretraining coverage as the cause. The runtime discussion also interprets the existing finetuning curve as a quality–computation tradeoff. Earlier reconstruction and trajectory-sampling limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the five DyCheck test sequences, specifies a 576 × 384 synthetic-benchmark input resolution and discloses the 140-minute cost of 400 finetuning steps. Existing optimizer, hardware, training-budget and project-access information is retained.

R1.justification: Six references are added on view synthesis, progressive generation and diffusion scaling. Sections 3–3.2 explicitly acknowledge similarities to Gen3C, TrajectoryCrafter and earlier training-data approaches, while retaining test-time finetuning as the central distinction.

P1.justification: Edits include the more explicit title, short runtime and viewing-angle discussions, acknowledgements, reference-format changes and small wording corrections. The overall section organization and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds runtime Table 3 and panoramic Figure 10, updates Figure 1's finetuning label and corrects its real-versus-generated caption. Several existing tables and figures shift position or numbering, while their underlying displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 3 makes the substantial test-time adaptation cost explicit, while Appendix B adds panoramic evidence and a concrete viewing-angle limitation. Clearer attribution also improves research positioning. These provide limited gains in transparency and applicability assessment, although the changed DyCheck resolution remains unexplained alongside identical reported scores.
